exposure: BMI categories: underweight (<18.5), normal weight (18.5-<25), overweight (25-<30), obese class I (30-<35), obese class II (35-<40), and obese class III (≥40)
cohort: 1,092,311 singleton deliveries in the state of Hesse in Germany from 1990 to 2012
finding: Maternal BMI in early pregnancy is linearly associated with the incidence of CD, with a disproportionate increase observed in morbidly obese women compared to the reference BMI population over the past two decades.
mod_finding: The study found a linear association between early-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) and the incidence of cesarean delivery.
